title: Hypergraph-Based Unaligned Multi-View Clustering via Cluster-Aware Feature Extraction

problem.claim: Unaligned multi-view clustering aims to mine distinct cluster structures from data whose sample features are not aligned across views.

gap.claim: Existing feature extraction strategies often neglect sample cluster structure, producing representations with ambiguous cluster distributions and causing suboptimal subsequent alignment and fusion.

contributions.claim: HG-UMC is a hypergraph-based cluster-aware alignment clustering framework that learns cluster-aware representations for subsequent alignment and fusion.

The Hyperedge-driven Feature Extraction module constructs multiple groups of learnable hyperedges to capture intrinsic sample clustering structure and incorporate it into hypergraph neural network feature extraction.

The Hyperedge-driven Cluster-level Alignment and Fusion module uses intra-cluster hyperedge similarity as cluster-specific topology and applies cluster-wise cross-attention for cross-view cluster-level fusion.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on various datasets verified HG-UMC's superiority over other state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: UMC targets clustering of unaligned multi-view data with distinct cluster structures.
Existing methods extract low-dimensional representations from high-dimensional raw features for alignment and fusion.
These strategies may ignore cluster structure, producing ambiguous cluster distributions and weaker downstream alignment and fusion.
HG-UMC introduces cluster-aware hypergraph feature extraction, followed by cluster-level alignment and cross-view fusion.
The authors report superiority over state-of-the-art methods on various datasets.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links ambiguous cluster distributions to downstream alignment and fusion problems.

interpretation.claim: When downstream integration depends on latent structure, preserving that structure during representation learning may improve later alignment.

application.claim: Design representation-learning stages that expose task-relevant group structure before cross-source alignment or fusion.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this lesson generalizes beyond unaligned multi-view clustering.
